problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{31}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$

feedback.problem: Determine the entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in the inverse of a matrix $A$ $=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$ if its determinant is $-2.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we want the entry ${a}_{12}^{′}$ in ${A}^{-1},$ we need to know the value of ${c}_{21}$ in the matrix of cofactors. For this, we use the formula to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{21} & =(-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(3-0) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, since ${A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{12}^{′}=\frac{1}{\text{det}(A)}{c}_{21}=\frac{1}{-2}\cdot (-3)=\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
